<color=red> !!! ACTIVATE THE TUTORIAL !!!</color>
Followers of the True Beaver Path, for them everything is a house. Their population often explodes out of control, food and water run out, science is a luxury, and your defeat unavoidable

 Forget what other factions taught you, and welcome to your pinkest nightmare.
<color=red> !!! ACTIVATE THE TUTORIAL !!!</color>

Your first district center, if it can be called so. Only dismantle after building a better town center.

"We can't go further, but we can settle here"
 -The expedition leader
A small and inefficient way to obtain mineral resources
"Beavers are not meant to dig rock"

A larger and deeper mine to exploit richer deposits, also gives access to rarer elements.
Comes with access stairs and barriers to prevent silly little kits from falling and getting hurt.
<color=green>Needs to be placed in a 4-deep hole!
Mine and fences must be on solid ground!
Place stairs on dirt spots and complete the access ramp</color>

"I don't believe in ghosts and monsters, what even are grues supposed to be anyway?"
 -Miner Zork, last words

A mixture of iron ore and coal in a clay crucible to be lit on fire.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>

A special fire pit to turn wood into charcoal.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>

"Oh, that would be a great way to get rid of... uhh... sawdust! Yes, sawdust... of course."
 -Jack the Gnawer

A strong press to extract oil from seeds, or juice from fruits.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
"Sunflower oil, essential for both salad and machines"

A cozy lab to prepare basic chemical reactions.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
"As long as we don't need a lot of that..."

A town house for copying existing blueprints. 
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"So the first part of my job, is to remove these ridiculous decorations"
 -The Copist beaver

A town house for decorating copied blueprints. 
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Yes, the blueprints MUST be fancy to be usable"
 -The artist beaver

A town house for two extra builders. 
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A small house for a hauler beaver.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
A semi-watertight structure built as the beavers of old used to.
A taller dam built on top of a previous one.
A bunch of logs arranged into primitive stairs.
"And that is why we need education" -A scientist beaver
A sorry excuse of a platform that is an embarrassment to beaverkind.
"And that too, is why we need education" -A scientist beaver
A crudely made but easy to build water wheel.

"With so much friction we're lucky it didn't catch on fire!"
 -An alchemist beaver

A medium house for two hauler beavers.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Can we even feed that many people?"
 -A farmer beaver

"Our population is getting out of paw"
 -The same farmer beaver
A primitive and inefficient tooth-powered sawmill.

"We really need to come up with a better solution"
 -A dentist beaver
A barely functional place to shape metal.
An old way to manufacture paper.

"It looks like some sort of soup"
 -Mathilda the insane cook

A powered sawmill using crude sawblades, with higher yield but consumes metal sawblades.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"This new technology is nice, but let's hope the blade doesn't break and hurt someone"
 -Mommy beaver

A sheltered place to grow mushroom from wood or sawdust.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>

"Should I eat this red-and-white one? Seems tasty"
 -Bobby the fool, last words

A tiny outdoor kitchen to prepare simple foods.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>

"What can we put inside? Ha! What can't we put inside?"
 -Mathilda the insane cook

A large mechanised kitchen to feed an entire colony. 
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
"Legend has it that one day a cook disappeared to never be found again"

"They look kind of tasty"
 -Bobby the fool

A fancy building to help architects show they're better than us. Also used to design structurally sound buildings. 
<color=green>Works as a big staircase</color>
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Architects are the worst."
 -An anonymous engineer beaver

A fancy building to help engineers show they're smarter than us. Also used to design mechanical buildings that work.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Engineers are the worst"
 -An anonymous architect beaver

A place to have fun in water.
If the pond does not already contain water, a <color=green>fluid dump</color> can be installed

Dumps water.
Must be built inside a <color=green>Lido</color>.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>
A pressurized tank to store gaz such as Methane or Hydrogen.
<color=green>got eaten up by heavy machinery and died</color>
<color=green>ventured into a dark tunnel and was eaten by a Grue</color>

"... and once a year on the darkest night, they open glowing eyes and mouths... to eat naughty little kits!"
 -Grandma beaver, campfire stories
Crude levee made of numerous logs stuck in the mud for basic landscaping. The flag must be entirely buried.

A tall house that doubles as a liquid storage.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"I... I tried, I really tried, but I couldn't help myself, I HAD to make it a house!"
 -An architect beaver

A tall house that doubles as a crate storage.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
"Modeled after the pinnacle of Hooman architecture: the cube"

"According to our archives, the traditional name goes back to some frog-eating hooman tribe"
 -Toothless the Wise, elder beaver

A large house for five hauler beavers.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Our population is getting out of paw"
 -The same farmer beaver

"We can make a full dam out of this!"
 -Toothless the Wise, elder beaver

« If only the tube wasn't so short… »
- A waterpumper beaver
Deep Water Pump Upgrade Terminal Segment

A watertight structure to block off the extremity of a chain of deep water pumps.
<color=red>Ram the camera into the building if placement is difficult</color>.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

« We make our dams the proper way, we're not savages! »
- The expedition leader

A watertight structure to block off the extremity of a chain of water pumps.
<color=red>Ram the camera into the building if placement is difficult</color>.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

« What if we just build that without the pump to block... Nah, that's a silly idea! »
- An engineer beaver
An easy to build gravity battery using a bunch of logs as weight.
A common punishment for kits is to be left dangling there for a few hours.
One day, the world will be completely covered with those.

"If you bite in it, you EAT it."
 -Grandma beaver
Think of how high we will be able to build with that!

« Aaah, civilisation comes back, at last! »
- A fermenter beaver
A somewhat tidy space to store resources properly.

"You called me for that ? There's nothing! No roof, no wall, nothing!"
 -A builder beaver
An embarrassing display of laziness applied to an unworthy task.

"I'm not wasting my time with that"
 -A builder beaver

"If you bite in it, you EAT it." 
-Grandma beaver

"What's cotton candy? Why does everyone call them "cotton candy tree"?"
 -A farmer beaver

"Did you know that fresh green peas are delicious?"
 -A mommy beaver

Pumps and filters water for beavers to drink.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
This beaver is covered in grime and refuses to work if it can't get cleaned up.
A protected river space for beaver to stir mud and prepare clay.

"Anything can be flammable waste, if you try hard enough."
 -The foundry overseer
A communal space for many beavers to meet and wash themselves after a long work day.

"I want the pink bucket!" "No it's mine, I always use it"
 -Typical kit squabbling

A small house monopolizing an excessive amount of material solely to allow one beaver to enjoy his hobby.
Might save your colony if you foolishly lost all of your berries or somehow managed to eradicate brambles.
The terrace must be <color=yellow>above ground.</color>
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"See, dandelions and berries like a very particular type of soil, very hard to replicate. That's why we can't plant them wherever we like."
 -A florist beaver

"I'm not scared of heights!"
 -Bobby the fool

"Working from home can sure be convenient, but once you start to have kits running around everywhere, a separate office is much better"
 -A builder beaver

"Why do I have to write down how many cabbages we have? Numbers are hard!"
 -Bobby the fool, on the concept of ''inventory''.

"As the heavy door slams shut behind you and your eyes slowly adjust to the dark, you can finally see the face of the mastermind threatening the world... With her mighty ladle of damnation in hand, Mathilda grins and says : "Do you want to BE stew?"
Now pass a terror check or take 2d6 damage! "

"We should think about using more machines for all this. Menial work will only get us so far."
 -An Engineer beaver

A medium house for a group of gatherer beavers to meet and split work efficiently.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Don't you dare come in my house covered in dirt and berry juice! Get a shower first or I'll toss you in the river myself!"
 -Mommy beaver, every evening.

A tall Lodge that doubles as a working hub for a group of lumberjacks, proper planning increasing their efficacy.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"My daddy's the strongest! He can carry a whole sequoia on his back!"
 -Typical kit boasting

A slightly enlarged lodge with a complicated waterlock system to allow beavers to easily access the other side of the dam.
Houses <color=green>one hauler</color> and its family.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
"You would think that this house has extra space right? Well no, the waterlock mechanism is huge and noisy. Thankfully almost no one uses it at night."
Harvests pine resin and other essences on some trees.
"It seems quite easy, but it requires some technique to not get your fur full of this sticky thing"

A complex device that masterfully transforms mechanical power into tasty food. 
Consumes wood for maintenance.

"The first rule of beaver engineering is to not look too closely at the mechanism"
 -Grandpa beaver, on what happened to his whiskers.

A mechanized paper factory.
Occasionally breaks a gear.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A mechanized drill that crushes rock to extract Iron ore.
The drill bits must be changed regularly.
<color=red>Deleting waste rock is cheating!</color>

"It's crazy how you can keep drilling the same spot for days and still find more!"
 -Mommy beaver

A mechanized drill that crushes rock to extract coal.
The drill bits must be changed regularly.
<color=red>Deleting waste rock is cheating!</color>

"If you spin the drill too fast, the coal might ignite and KABOOM the mountain!"
 -A bad alchemist beaver

"If you need an anvil to make other anvils, where does the first anvil come from?"
 -Armok, metalworker beaver

A big house set to allow brewers to easily manage a large number of fermentation barrels.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Mushroom juice is the worst-tasting thing you could think of, and yet adding it to some preparations makes everything better. We should study this someday"
 -A scientist beaver
"No Bobby, you fell inside when you where little, remember?"
"If you wait long enough, you can climb it to reach the moon!"

« Did you know that purple stew works as an amazing fertiliser ? »
- A tree nursery worker
Stores giant logs from golden sequoias.
"How did he manage to carry that all this way?"
Cuts down giant sequoias and stores a few giants logs.
"I guess if it falls on my face I won't have to worry about the taste of the hospital food"
Who doesn't need a good old trebuchet?

A large house where a live-in nurse tends to wounded beavers.
Treats benign conditions with twice the efficacy of a medical bed.
Can also manufacture advanced medicine to treat severe conditions.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A large billboard that displays information relative to the latest update.
Can be placed above cabbages.
A deep storage facility that use the ground itself as thermal insulation.

"The best place to store ice, ice cream, or corpses! ... Why are you looking at me like that? YOU brought this disgusting stuff back!"
 - Jack the gnawer
This beaver has been badly hurt, this won't heal without proper treatment.
This beaver got burned and should go rest.
<color=green>caught on fire and died due to extreme carelessness. Turns out furry creatures are quite flammable.</color>
This beaver got severely burned at his job, this won't heal without treatment.
<color=green>fell into a pool of molten material shouting "My prreeeciouuuus". It was acting really strange lately.</color>
This beaver is sick and should go rest.
<color=green>'s condition suddenly worsened and is now free of suffering. Let's hope it was not contagious.</color>
This beaver caught something nasty, this won't heal without treatment.
<color=green>contracted what can only be described as ''everything''. Doctors took the hard decision to put him down after it started growing a third head.</color>
This poor beaver lost a limb working a dangerous job! It will need a prosthetic so it can again live a normal life.
Stores precious core items and displays them on a glorious pillow.
Surely the best way to store a unique and vital set of glassware.

"So we have to refill the lights when the player's not look-
 - Shhhh! That's a secret!"
 -Two anonymous beavers

"Come on! Stop acting like a kit! Danger? What danger? I laugh at the face of danger! Ah-Ah-Ah-Arghbllglblbglbl"
 -Ruin exploration team Nb 3, team leader's last words.

A tall and narrow lodge for one hauler.
Useful to dam narrow corners.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Ugh, who thought this would be livable? This gotta be an architect's work!"
 -An engineer beaver

"Definitely the best use of limited resources..."
 -The expedition leader.

<color=red>This thing is deprecated and misses some new functionality!
Replace it with a new one when you get the chance.</color>

<color=red>This building is deprecated and misses some new functionality!
Replace it with a new one when you get the chance.</color>

"I wonder if I can get into the barrel just before it starts shooting..."
 -Yet another silly beaver
Captures sunlight and turns it into this weird "electricity" thing according to ancient hooman texts. Better keep an eye on it, and an other eye on where you step.

"Eheh, the fun part is to cook slices of pumpkins on the hot surfaces in summer"
- the array supervising beaver

A shower that takes its water from a storage barrel.
Mostly useful for the unhinged weirdos who can't help but try to play on hard mode.
Accomodates 2 beavers.
Why are you doing this to yourself?

Plants basic trees.
<color=#FFA500>Small Tower</color>, <color=#FF6EC7>Can support upgrades</color>
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A town house where manufactured items are made.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

Irrigates land around by consuming water.
<color=green>Water consumption is barely higher than a water dump.</color>
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A medium lodge managing a lovely terrace where beavers can get a fresh drink.
The terrace must be <color=yellow>above ground.</color>
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A large house equipped with a mechanized kitchen to feed many beavers.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

An upgrade module to be placed between two adjacent water pumps.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
<color=green>Placement is sensitive to camera orientation!</color>

An upgrade module to be placed between two adjacent deep water pumps.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
<color=green>Placement is sensitive to camera orientation!</color>

An enormous building that could dam a whole river by itself.
Cuts giant logs into different products.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"I'll only be satisfied once I've cut the world in half"
 - A mechanic beaver

Allows beavers to go down into the ruins and explore an ancient hooman facility.
Truly the adventure of a lifetime. What dark secrets will we find down there?

A gigantic pot meant to be placed on a fire to keep food warm.
<color=green>Placement is sensitive to camera orientation!</color>

"But... how...? This thing is bigger than a house!
 -An architect beaver
A wood-consuming storage structure meant to hold and keep warm a large amount of cooked food.

"Apparently the hoomans used to say that every good game needs a paw-shaped building. But why did we decide to build that in real life?"
 -Mathilda, pre-insanity days.
"A jail for beavers made entirely of wood seems a silly idea, but they're just too polite to escape"

A medium-sized lodge for one hauler, built around a ladder.
Manages a box storage space.
Can be stacked on itself, variants, and can carry select buildings.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"If you paint the whole tower green and go down the ladder from the top, you will end up in a strange world filled with walking mushrooms and flying turtles!"
 -Mathilda the insane cook

A medium-sized lodge for one hauler, built around a ladder.
Manages a tank of liquid storage.
Can be stacked on itself, variants, and can carry select buildings.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Architects must have had severe constraints on this thing to accept making it simple and functional."
 -An engineer beaver
Pit & Ladder Lodge (Haulers With Side Door)

A medium-sized lodge for two haulers, built around a ladder.
Can be stacked on itself, variants, and can carry select buildings.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Thanks to the latest development in bucket technology, water won't even get inside the central pit!"
 -BeavX technologies CEO

A medium-sized lodge for two haulers, built around a ladder.
Can be stacked on itself, variants, and can carry select buildings.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"I wonder how high we can go with that..."
 -A lumberjack beaver

An entirely mechanical bad water pumping station.
The propeller needs to be submerged.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"The modmaker is a sadistic maniac? What's a ''modmaker''? What are you talking about? Did you drink that stuff?"
 -A worried nurse beaver
<color=red>Sprotch! No one should ever see this message</color>

A billboard displaying the technological progression of the WhitePaws faction.
Useful to know if you're attempting to build something waaaaay out of reach.
Also displays what is made where.
"What wouldn't beaverkind do for something to spice up life?"
Pit & Ladder Lodge (Builders With Side Door)

A medium-sized watertight lodge built around a ladder, with a side access door.
Can be stacked on itself, variants, and can carry select buildings.
Employs <color=green>three builders</color>.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Building up like that sure is convenient, but aren't we doing the same things as the hoomans?"
 -A concerned carpenter beaver

A medium-sized watertight lodge built around a ladder, but without side door for aesthetic reasons.
Can be stacked on itself, variants, and can carry select buildings.
Employs <color=green>three builders</color>.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A bizarre contraption meant to wash and decontaminate beavers using mechanical power.
Half of the effect is actually due to purging beaver's stomachs.

A crappy bath built with logs, deliberately made leaky in order to use the dirty water for irrigation.
Mostly useful for the unhinged weirdos who can't help but try to play this on hard mode despite having been told not to.

"We should get a proper dam built, because this won't last"
 -A farmer beaver
This beaver got its daily treatment.
An artificial terrain block built by beavers as an useful way to get rid of excess dirt generated by the <color=red>mechanical drill</color>

A small platform attached to a wall in order to form a walkway.
<color=green>Can be attached to the sides of cliffs and most stackable buildings</color>
<color=red>Multiple side platforms or bridges cannot share the same support</color>

A small, manually-operated bad water pumping station.
Possibly designed by a deranged beaver.
The propeller needs to be submerged.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Why would anyone design something like this? Younglings these days..."
 -Toothless the Wise, elder beaver
<color=green>thought it would be hilarious to hide in the trebuchet basket. To be fair it was.</color>

A building specialized in preparing purified components from natural or manufactured resources.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Can't the alchemist just do that too?"
 -Mommy beaver
Please do not obstruct the blades with branches, logs, or the bodies of your vanquished enemies.

An intriguing evolution of the mechanical water pump of other factions. 
Shoots water at a 70° angle for ranged irrigation.
Allows to send water high up but at short range.
<color=green>The cannon will fill the reservoir up to the blue flag</color>

An intriguing evolution of the mechanical water pump that shoots water at a 30° angle for ranged irrigation.
Maximizes range at the expense of elevation
<color=green>Cannon will continue working until the water level reaches the blue flag</color>

An intriguing evolution of the mechanical water pump that shoots water at a 45° angle for ranged irrigation.
Provides a good balance between range and elevation.
<color=green>Cannon will continue working until the water level reaches the blue flag</color>
Now we just need chocolate and ice cream...

A large greenhouse to keep banana trees warm and happy
<color=red>Crushable building! Be careful! Only allows banana trees!
This building is not watertight!</color>

"If you eat only bananas, you won't wear your teeth down and eventually they will grow so long that they will go through your skull"
 -Mommy beaver
The only realistic way to get rid of all those useless rocks. Also allows that one nerdy beaver to study ballistics.
A few logs and planks haphazardly arranged in a platform barely good enough to tap bad water with a bucket, hopefully without sullying oneself.

"I'm sure we can do something useful with this liquid, we just need someone foolish enough to accept getting it. Surely Bobby will be up to the task."
 -A scientist beaver

A pile of barrels that can be filled with different things that are left to ferment, pickle or decompose.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>

"A closed space that no one ever opens? Interesting..."
 -Jack the Gnawer

A large industrial building for melting metal into steel and manufacturing order-made items.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A specialized building in which experienced forester beavers carefully tend to tiny saplings and grow exotic species before planting them outside.
<color=red>The house body can connect from the bottom to a ladder or pit-and-ladder lodge.</color>
A bigger, more efficient water wheel, supported from the side.

An advanced science institute for the brightest beavers to develop new technologies
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

An unusual workplace reserved for the most fearless beavers. Grows giant carnivorous fireflies from tiny larvae in order to harvest the glowing fluid from their abdomen. The ravenous beast is kept attached at all times to make the process perfectly safe.

"You see kits: every bad thing has its silver lining! Tending to those is quite easy, and what's it gonna do? Eat my prosthetic arm? Ha!"
 -Grandpa beaver, on how to live a happy life.
<color=green>didn't know what ''carnivorous'' meant and tried to pet a giant firefly, proving that it is always better to ask your questions to the teacher</color>

Half a sequoia artistically fitted into a not-half sequoia to provide a walkway.
Comes with lights underneath because no one wants to live in total darkness.

"This doesn’t look very stable…"
 -A farmer beaver

An enclosed place to grow genetically modified mushrooms or plants in optimal condition, resulting in incredible yields and growth speed.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"Should I eat this red-and-white mushroom? It seems tasty."
 -Bobby the fool, last words.

A complex device that masterfully transforms mechanical power into logs.
The sawblades must be changed regularly.

"The first rule of beaver engineering is to not look too closely at the mechanism"
 -Grandpa beaver, on what happened to his whiskers.

"And... what do you need the platform for, exactly?"
 -A confused lumberjack beaver

A tall hourglass-shaped centrifuge used to purify nuclear fuel from hooman nuclear waste.
Also acts as a somewhat impractical dwelling for the sake of upholding tradition.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
Thankfully, some beavers are capable of sleeping even in the most unlikely circumstances.

An oversized press using nuclear heat to hot squeeze more oil out of sunflower seeds.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

A small lodge whose inhabitants are tasked with supplying and taking care of the fermentation barrels installed in the upper floor.
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

"No one will notice if I keep some extra for myself..."
 -A fermenter beaver

An old tower design repurposed to serve as a gargantuan storage for warm food.
Heat is provided for free and forever by a massive rod of low grade radioactive matter in the center of the tower.

"Even better, the food placed in there never rots, and the fools that supply it never have kits!"
 -An eugenicist beaver
A complex but extremely convenient dam piece which wall can be raised or lowered to control water flow.

"If you find a black one, you can sell it to the nerds for thousands of cabbages!"
 -A farmer beaver
Irrigating Elevated Public Bath Fancy Blueprint
Irrigating Elevated Public Bath Fancy Blueprints
A small storage place for one scroll that serves to facilitate importation of blueprints from other districts.

A small watertight house that controls a sluice.
Allows the dam to not completely block the water flow.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>

Burns Methane to create power.
<color=#00FFFF>Works as a Levee</color>
Gives injured beavers a place to rest while someone adjust the <color=green>basic balm</color> into a <color=green>pine resin</color> cataplasm.
Gives beavers suffering from burns a place to rest while someone adjust the <color=green>basic balm</color> into an oily <color=green>sunflower seed</color>-based ointment.
Gives sick beavers a place to rest while someone adjust the <color=green>basic balm</color> into a relieving <color=green>bramble flower</color> decoction.

"If people keep thinking irrigation towers are lame, just keep making them better until they like them!"
 -A carpenter beaver.

The ultimate irrigation tower: An elevated bath that irrigates crops with the dirty water, fertilizing them for faster growth, all the while having a minimal land pawprint.
<color=green>Water consumption scales with irrigated area.
Plant growth +15%</color>
<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>

Sends down the abyss a team of beavers specialized in ancient hooman machinery to repair and reactivate manufacturing tools that are far above our own technological level.
<color=#FF6EC7>Tasks that would have required an entire day for specialized craftbeavers can now be completed multiple times in barely a few hours.</color>
"Apparently one of the hoomans' greatest fears was to see their own machines rebel against them, how silly is that? How could this big hunk of metal ev- Ouch! It zapped me!"
A mechanized pump that can exploit pockets of various gases identified by the exploration teams.
"You wouldn't imagine how many different smells there is down there..."
Repurposes an empty sector of the abandoned hooman facility to store an excessive amount of resources.

"This thing is so immense that we could spend a lifetime exploring it"
-An explorer beaver

"Why did they need all this space? Were they planning to live there? To survive their own man-made apocalypse?"
-An explorer beaver
Sends down the abyss a team of beavers specialized in recovering the strange warm stuff the hoomans buried down there so long ago, so that it can be refined again into something useful.
"Exploring? No no no... that's not my job, I do this one because I don’t want to be killed by some devious thing I can’t see."
Combined Rice Alcohol Fermentation and Distillation

Organizes guided tours in safe and already explored sectors of the hooman derelict facility.
Guaranteed 100% Grue-free.
"Who doesn't like the thrill of maybe being eaten by a grue, without actually being eaten by a grue?"

Sends down the abyss a team of chemist beavers to study and reactivate an ancient hooman chemical plant.
<color=#FF6EC7>Their processes were far more advanced than ours - we will surely learn so much! </color>
"Manufacturing resin entirely from base elements? This is amazing!"

A half-barn, half-lodge building used as a workplace for a group of lumberjacks. Contains a few tools to help them do their job efficiently.
Has a <color=#FF6EC7>triangle roof</color>, <color=#FF6EC7>Can support upgrades</color>

Dear Expedition Leader,

If you are reading this, you have either discovered a promising site for settlement… or, far more plausibly, stranded yourself in the middle of nowhere after exercising the exceptional judgment for which you are widely known.

We will send instructions on how to establish a viable colony. We strongly encourage you to follow them precisely, as improvisation is unlikely to improve your current situation.

Do try not to doom the industrious, optimistic, and tragically trusting individuals you convinced to accompany you into exile. Their only mistake was believing you.

Should the settlement fail, please ensure the failure remains local.

Remember that this expedition is equal parts your punishment and an experiment.

Do not come back.

Establish three Lumberjack Flags, one Gatherer’s Flag, and one Tapper’s Flag. If this instruction feels obvious, that is because it is.

Trees will provide logs. Bushes will provide berries. Pine trees, when properly tapped, will provide resin — assuming you have the patience to let them live long enough.

We trust you can identify a tree without assistance.

Now that you have demonstrated the ability to recognize a tree, we may proceed to more advanced concepts.

Build a Water Pump. Water is essential for survival, despite what certain “visionaries” have previously attempted to prove.

Establish a Farmhouse and plant cabbages. We recommend cabbages because they are resilient, dependable, and unlikely to wander off — qualities we value highly in a colony.

Try to ensure your settlers drink before they dehydrate and eat before they starve. Timing is important.

A brief precaution.

You may have noticed that the local brambles possess an admirable enthusiasm for expansion. Unlike your expedition plans, they spread efficiently and without hesitation.

Before they overtake your entire settlement — which they will — pause your operations and construct at least one Fence Gate and four sections of Fence to contain them.

We recommend acting sooner rather than later, unless you wish to conduct future correspondence from inside a shrub.

A Matter of Standards

We Whitepaws take great pride in our immaculate coats. Cleanliness is not a luxury — it is a reflection of who we are.

Construct a River Bath in the river, or provide Showers if you insist on engineering where nature would suffice.

Be advised: a Whitepaw who cannot get cleaned up will go on strike. Negotiations rarely improve the situation.

We know you enjoy a good riot.

You will find it significantly less amusing when you are the target.

A brief clarification, lest you attempt to imitate our cousins the Folktails.

We Whitepaws do not separate labor from shelter when it can be avoided. Most of our workplaces also serve as lodgings, and most of our lodgings are <color=#00FFFF>watertight</color>. We are beavers : our dams are our houses, and our houses are our dams. This is the law.

You may notice these structures “<color=#00FFFF>work as levees</color>.”

To ensure stability and modest growth, construct a second Farmhouse, a second Water Pump, and one Forester.

These additions will bring your settlement to fifteen beds. With adequate housing, new births may follow.

Their fate will also be your responsibility

You will now address storage.

Construct appropriate facilities to contain your growing supplies. Disorder is the first sign of failure.

Build a Log Pile for timber. Build storage for Pine Resin. It may appear unnecessary at present. It will soon be required.

Rice, despite sentimental objections you may invent, is to be stored in a Pile like any other granular resource. Coal does not complain. Dirt does not complain. Rice will adapt.

You may feel the urge to construct a dam. This instinct is understandable. It is also premature.

Building a proper semi-permeable dam would require metal fixtures that we currently do not have. We need to wait and endure.

Construct four Small Water Tanks and two Pit Tanks. Store water while it still flows.

We must address your so-called “District Center.”

Take a moment to observe it. Yes — that pile of splintered wood and disappointed debris. That is not an administrative hub. That is evidence of your personnality.

To establish a proper District Center, you will require Planks. Logs alone do not constitute progress.

Construct a Log Gnawing Station to process timber into planks. In addition, build appropriate storage for Planks and for Sawdust.

We sent you to found a new town, not to camp beside a traffic accident.

A note regarding Sawdust.

Your Log Gnawing Station will soon produce it in quantities exceeding aesthetic value. Left unattended, it will accumulate, obstruct operations, and quietly undermine your efficiency.

Fortunately, sawdust is still wood. It can be used to cultivate Mushrooms in a Mushroom Grower.

There are two accepted methods:
– A faster process using sawdust directly.
– A slower method using whole logs.

Which is superior is an old and moldy debate, and does not yield mushrooms.

Do both, fungi are patient. Your settlers are not.

You may have noticed that certain buildings <color=#FF6EC7>can function without workers.</color>. This does not mean deliveries will arrive magically.

Construct a Lodge to provide dedicated Haulers. Other structures capable of housing haulers are equally acceptable. The important matter is that someone carries what must be carried.

You will also recall that our block-formed buildings are watertight. This is not decorative, consider placing the Lodge directly within the river. Narrowing the current now will simplify future dam construction.

We are beavers. Every structure is an opportunity to reshape the river.

A word on priorities.

You have access to five levels of urgency. This does not mean you are expected to use “Maximum” as a personality trait.

Assign Maximum Priority <color=red>only</color> to the Farms and Water Pumps. Food and water sustain the colony. Without them, other concerns resolve themselves rather quickly.

The Forester is important. It is not urgent. Set it to High Priority, not Maximum.

If everything is critical, nothing is.

Your settlers can only be in one place at a time. We trust this is not new information.

A colony is not defined by how many buildings it possesses, but by how many it can meaningfully operate.

Certain structures, including the Woodburner and the Mushroom Growers, are capable of functioning without constant supervision. As stated previously, they indicate:

<color=#FF6EC7>Can function without workers.</color>

Set both Mushroom Growers to Minimal Priority, as well as any <color=green>Woodburner</color> or <color=green>Primitive Smelter</color> you may have built while ignoring our pleas not to improvise.

To ensure materials are still delivered, set your Lodge (employing the hauler) to High Priority.

Lastly, you may want to lower the priority of the <color=green>Log Gnawing Station</color> and/or <color=green>Primitive Mine</color>. This way, they will operate only when the workforce is abundant.

If everything runs at all times, then nothing runs when it matters.

It seems you have managed to secure the basic necessities. Survival, however, is not the same as refinement.

With <color=green>Mushrooms</color> and <color=green>Cabbages</color>, you may now prepare <color=green>Braised Cabbage</color> — a meal properly cooked rather than merely harvested. You will find that cooking produces more nourishment than the simple sum of its ingredients.

This is not magic. It is organization.

To begin, construct a Clay Pit and extract Clay. Civilized meals require proper vessels, and proper vessels require proper materials.

Clay is stored in boxes, should you be interested in such trivia.

We Whitepaws do not merely survive. We dine.

Having secured clay, you will now require fire.

Construct a Woodburner. It will harden clay into usable materials, logs may be transformed into <color=green>Coal</color> and, should your enthusiasm for Planks exceed your foresight, dispose of excess <color=green>Sawdust</color>.

When placing the Woodburner, note that its entrance is on the first floor. Your convenience matters little to engineers.

<color=green>Set the building to fabricate clay pots</color>.

Fire elevates a settlement from survival to industry. Use it carefully.

With clay pots prepared, you may now construct a Cooking Tent.

Build the Cooking Tent and begin preparing Braised Cabbage.

Cooked meals sustain morale. Morale increases productivity. Increased productivity compensates for your mistakes.

Clay Pots, once fired, are not to be discarded carelessly among common goods.

Construct a Glorious Storage to house them properly. Certain items deserve presentation and display. We are not savages.

That said, restraint is advised. A modest supply of clay pots will suffice.

Braised Cabbage, once prepared, is not meant to cool into disappointment. Go ahead and try if you don’t believe us.

To preserve warmth, you must first construct the Hand of Soup. This clay structure serves as a fire pit and foundation. Heat must come from somewhere.

Upon it, build the Warm Storage — the bowl in which meals are kept heated and ready for distribution.

The Hand may be oriented left or right. Choose wisely. Crimes against symmetry shall be punished.

The Library requires a considerable quantity of planks. Gnawing logs into shape will suffice for now, but we prefer progress to dental heroics.

You may therefore consider constructing a Rudimentary Sawmill. It is faster, more efficient, and considerably less embarrassing.

However, the sawmill requires Power.

To understand how to connect power properly, place the <color=green>Billboard</color>: “How to Connect Power.”

Actually building the billboard is not required. Placing it, is.
Please do not question how this works.

We recommend observing it carefully, keep in mind that shaft plugs and windows are, in fact, no the same.

Having consulted the instructional billboard, you may now construct the Rudimentary Sawmill.

In most circumstances, one or two Crappy Waterwheels will suffice to power it. Position them in flowing water. We trust you can identify flowing water without assistance.

Should you be fortunate enough to settle near a <color=green>Geothermal Field</color>, a <color=green>Geothermal Engine</color> is also acceptable.

However you choose to power it, ensure the sawmill is supplied with <color=green>sawblades</color>, those are made by the workers of your <color=green>primitive ironworks</color> who surely regret following you by now.

Should you decide to build a stock of those, sawblades are stored in piles.

Should you not have done so already, you may now connect your power source to the Sawmill.

If you encounter difficulty, consult again the <color=green>“How to Connect Power” billboard</color>. Unlike… someone… it did not seize the first opportunity to run away.

The sawmill’s shaft plug is located on the rear side of the structure — ground floor, to the right. Hopefully you noticed this before actually building it.

Unlike some savages, we do not run power shafts through our living rooms.

Your Rudimentary Sawmill should now be operational. Observe its yield.

Each log produces two planks, at greater speed, and with less sawdust generated in the process. This is what we mean by progress.

Construct six Plank Tanks. They are significantly more efficient than the small water tanks you assembled in haste.

If resources are limited, dismantling your existing small tanks to reclaim the logs is acceptable.

Temporary solutions should remain temporary.

While you were certainly scattering yourself on several self-inflicted tasks, your Log Gnawing Station should have produced sufficient planks to construct a proper District Center.

Build the new center <color=red>before</color> dismantling the original. Your builders work from the cart, removing it prematurely would make them very upset.

When you do dismantle the cart, several important items will be released into the debris. They are marked with <color=red>red icons</color>. 

Red usually indicates importance. We trust this concept is familiar. These are not decorative and – in fact – vital for the success of your colony.

<color=green>Ensure these materials are collected before the rubble disappears.</color>

Among the contents recovered from the dismantled cart, you may have noticed several sticks of <color=green>Dynamite</color>.

You are free to use these explosives as you see fit. We recommend doing so wisely, but who are we kidding ?

Prepare an adequate storage for explosives. In case you have forgotten, common sense says to keep them in a dry, covered, and locked building.

Among the recovered materials from the cart, you will have secured an <color=green>Anvil</color>.

With it, you may construct a Primitive Ironworks — and with ironworks, we may finally speak of real engineering.

To supply it, establish a Scavenger Flag and begin collecting Scrap Metal from nearby ruins.

In addition, construct a Primitive Mine. It may extract Iron Ore or Coal, both of which can be refined into scrap metal within an <color=green>Ore Smelter</color>. Alternatively, coal can be obtained from the <color=green>woodburner</color>, should your tendency to destroy the environment have already got the best of you.

With this, you can at last build a proper dam and make droughts easier on your people.

Accidentally, you might even make your mother proud. And surpised.

With mining operations underway, you will require proper storage for raw materials.

Construct a Large Pile for Iron Ore, and another for Coal.

If mined minerals remain stored inside the mine, have they truly been mined?

You have secured water, food, and iron. This is acceptable.

It is now time to pursue something rarer: knowledge.

Among the items recovered from the cart was an <color=green>Incredibly Compact Library Set</color>. We dare to hope you did not mistake it for dried food.

Start construction of a Library. It will take time to complete. Scholarship rarely tolerates haste.

Once operational, it will allow the generation of Science, and with science, progress beyond improvisation.

Your Library is now under construction, hopefully you chose a sensible location. Knowledge does not emerge from architecture alone. Study requires three elements: sustenance, hydration… and stimulation. To supply the latter, you must obtain Badwater. For now, construct a Badwater Bucketing Post and begin collection from your environment. This task carries certain health risks. Exposure causes illness, if anyone, you should remember. Build the appropriate facility. Surely you remember from experience the right treatment, do not make us spell it out.

A studying session would only yield boredom if not supplemented with snacks, and by snacks we mean <color=green>Kimchi</color>.

To produce Kimchi, you will need <color=green>Bramble Flowers</color>, they are harvested by Lumberjacks. However, the task is… extensive. Assigning unqualified flag workers to the task would condemn them to a tedious and prickly existence.

Construct a Woodfelling Planification Lodge or a Lumberjack’s Barn near brambles so that properly qualified workers can take care of it. Qualified workers get a little hat, that is how you know they are qualified.

Also, <color=red>mark the brambles for cutting</color>. They will not volunteer.

Those buildings will require <color=green>Tools</color>. These are fabricated in the <color=green>Primitive Ironworks</color>. Competence works better with equipment.

While this is getting done, construct three stacks of Fermentation Barrels. Patience will convert sharpness into nourishment.

Only psychopaths would snack on Kimchi all day. Sane beavers will also require <color=green>Sunflower Seeds</color> and <color=green>Berries</color> to munch on.

Plant Sunflowers if you have not done so already.

Construct appropriate storage for the seeds. As with Rice — and all other granular materials — they are to be kept in a Pile.

We are aware that certain heretics prefer to box them up. Our seeds have not committed any crime yet.

Your Foresters are probably still unable to plant new berry bushes. This is a recurring issue in new settlements.

<color=green>Protect the ones you have as much as possible</color>.

Snacks alone do not make a genius out of a fool, and we have reason to believe your team may be short on geniuses. Fortunately, certain mushrooms continue to grow in the toxic sludge known as Badwater, and these specimens possess… useful properties. No, they do not cause visions of flying hoomans. Nor do they induce spontaneous joy. They primarily enhance focus, memory, and imagination. They also occasionally cause you-know-what. Manage it accordingly. Construct a third Mushroom Grower and configure it to cultivate Brain-Stimulating Mushrooms. Prepare suitable storage as well. Intellectual advancement should not be left on the ground.

As stated previously, attempts at replanting <color=green>berries</color> are often unsuccessful. Yet they remain necessary.

Should your supply prove insufficient — whether by neglect or enthusiastic removal — berries may also be cultivated by a Florist.

Note that each Florist has a small terrace in front of it for growing flowers. Surprising, isn't it?

This terrace must rest above ground level, or atop structures without a roof such as paths, piles, or warehouses. Common sense would also suggest leaving sufficient clearance above the plants.

Place two Florists to familiarize yourself with their arrangement. <color=green>You may pause or dismantle them later</color>.

The Florist is capable of more than berry cultivation. Most notably, it can produce <color=green>Plant Fibers</color>.

Fibers, when properly spun into <color=green>Rope</color>, enable construction techniques unavailable to the unprepared — <color=green>suspension bridges</color>, <color=green>rope stairs</color>, and <color=green>ziplines</color> among them.

To process fibers, place a Handicrafter.

The Handicrafter may also be tasked with producing other useful items, including properly assembled <color=green>explosives</color>, should the need for decisive terrain modification arise.

Place one Handicrafter to familiarize yourself with its function. <color=green>You may pause or dismantle it later</color>.

With the Library nearing completion, it is time to prepare for written scholarship.

Among the recovered items from the cart was a <color=green>Metal Cauldron</color>. Such vessels are commonly associated with cooking, but we will apply it to a higher purpose.

The few promising minds unfortunate enough to have been born in your... general vicinity... will require something better than bark and flat rocks upon which to record their ideas.

Construct a Primitive Papermill. Within it, sawdust and pine resin are boiled together to produce <color=green>paper</color> in the traditional manner.

You may have noticed that sawdust now fuels mushroom cultivation, artificial soil for the florist, and soon, paper production. <color=green>It is no longer waste</color>, use it wisely.

It appears the necessary preparations have been established.

The Library now only needs to be completed.

Maintain stable supply lines while the work concludes.

You are still alive. Interesting.

With the Library operational, your settlement may now generate Science.

Accumulate 100 Science Points. This will mark the transition from improvisation to planification.

Should you find it difficult to maintain a steady supply of Berries and Sunflower Seeds for study — particularly if other beavers insist on consuming them recreationally — consider preparing <color=green>Cereal Bars</color> in the <color=green>Cooking Tent</color>.

Properly prepared, they satisfy both desires more efficiently than the raw ingredients.

Scholars require provisions. So do opportunists.

You have secured water, industry, scholarship, and structured governance.

This is… satisfactory.

Reaching this stage of development exceeds several internal projections. As a consequence, certain parties within this bureau are now wealthier than they were previously. Others seem distressed at your success for unexplained reasons.

We assure you there was no wager placed on your odds of long-term survival. Officially.

You may now proceed with greater autonomy. The settlement is stable enough to pursue multiple avenues of advancement. <color=green>Four principal paths stand before you</color>.

Explore them as you see fit. They are not mutually exclusive. In fact, you are expected to explore all of them eventually.

Continue.

You may have learned at school that there are irregularities in the water cycle. These are not temporary inconveniences.

<color=red>Badtides</color> will come. When they do, every flowing body of water will turn hostile.

Water must be disciplined before it disciplines you.

<color=green>Follow up on this letter as soon as you are able to</color>. We will guide you in securing your settlement against this scourge and restoring order to the river.

Panic is common. It is also inefficient.

Your correspondence has been received.

The timing is appropriate. Conditions suggest an elevated probability of environmental instability. We recommend immediate preparatory action.

Begin by constructing at least one Irrigation Tower.

Placement is strategic. Install it <color=green>on dry land you wish to cultivate</color>, <color=#00FFFF>near riverbanks vulnerable to contamination</color>, or both.

By default, the tower irrigates surrounding soil. This is useful. It is insufficient.

When supplied with <color=green>Pollution Resistance Factor</color>, the tower’s field effect will repel soil contamination originating from badwater. This is preferable.

Construct a Distillery to manufacture Pollution Resistance Factor. It is stored in tanks, like any other liquid. It may also be used as a basic treatment against badwater poisoning.

Hydrological events cannot be prevented. Their consequences can.

Your badwater readiness level is improving. Let us continue.

Protecting your farmland is essential, but for us Whitepaws, who live in constant wetness, letting badwater flow freely through your village is unacceptable.

A disciplined river must be given instructions. To that end, you must now begin construction of a proper dam.

In most circumstances, wisdom dictates beginning with a Valve Lodge at the base of your future dam. These structures allow you to regulate the passage of water.

The Valve Lodge requires <color=green>Gears</color>. Several should have been recovered from the cart. If they have been allocated elsewhere, additional gears may be produced in a <color=green>Mechanic’s Lodge</color>.

With irrigation and contamination control established, we may now address proper dam construction.

You may have noticed that most watertight buildings in Whitepaw settlements possess flat, reinforced roofs. This is our urban planning doctrine: structures should remain stackable whenever possible.

Construct six Water Pumps. If possible, place them in a row <color=green>above your Valve Lodge</color>. Feel free to raze older water pumps if they have outlived their usefulness.

These buildings are <color=#00FFFF>watertight</color> and will therefore reinforce the dam, increasing its retention height by one additional level.

Be advised:  <color=red>using buildings as dam elements without operating them—leaving them permanently paused, unconnected, or otherwise decorative—is considered asevere violation of Whitepaw construction law</color>. Do not do that unless you want to be visited by the Gesta-Paw.

If you do not yet have access to <color=green>Platforms</color> from the Architect’s Lodge, you may construct <color=green>Florists</color> beneath the pumps. Their terraces provide convenient walkways for maintenance, and their structures will further increase the dam’s retention height.

Your dam will allow to store water despite droughts, but do not forget to leave an outflow for bad water to be evacuated, preferably away from your settlement.

The rest is up to you, good luck.

Progress produces byproducts. Some are useful. Some are volatile.

The responsible settlement studies both.

This branch concerns chemical refinement, <color=green>healthcare</color>, and the controlled application of <color=red>explosive</color> solutions where geography requires punishment.

When you are prepared to handle substances that sting your snout, follow up on this directive.

Destroying obstacles is a form of construction.

Ah! Excellent. Someone finally contacted us.

A functioning settlement that managed to assemble a library is bound to see its workforce suffer the usual assortment of burns, infections, and poorly judged actions that goes with everyday life. Perfectly normal.

To address these matters, you will need an Alchemist.

The Alchemist requires <color=green>Laboratory Glassware</color>. One set should have been recovered from the cart. Hopefully it has not been misplaced, broken, or otherwise involved in an experiment of questionable supervision.

You have only one set, and it is vital. This means you will be limited to a single Alchemist for now.

Once operational, the Alchemist can prepare <color=green>Basic Balm</color>, a reliable compound for treating minor injuries, burns, and other predictable consequences of industrial progress.

Do try to keep the workers alive. They are useful for further experiments.

Excellent. With Basic Balm available, we may begin addressing the more common consequences of having fun.

Construct at least one Medical Bed. There are three varieties, each specialized for a different category of minor ailment. Select whichever seems most relevant to the circus you are currently running.

Basic Balm is not usable as-is; it must be adjusted directly at the bed into the appropriate medication. The procedure is simple and well documented.

Do not attempt to modify the formulation. We already tried that. The results involved a traumatic amount of paperwork and several new laws being passed.

Medical beds are suitable for minor ailments only. Severe cases require a <color=green>Clinic</color>, staffed by a beaver with <color=green>proper medical training</color>.

Since you clearly do not have anyone fitting that description, you will need to lock a few volunteers in the <color=green>library</color> and make do with the least incompetent one who eventually emerges.

Excellent. Your Alchemist can now prepare basic medicine, but actual chemistry requires something more fundamental.

<color=green>Oil</color>.

Oil is a remarkably cooperative substance. It fuels industry, improves cooking, seals structures, and participates in several reactions that we are very excited to discuss later.

Construct a Screwpress to extract oil from Sunflower Seeds.

The press operates through a <color=green>Screw Axle</color>, which will gradually wear down under pressure. Replacement axles can be manufactured in the <color=green>Log Gnawing Station</color>. We recommend keeping a few spare parts available.

If you catch some of your townsfolk having fun crushing things with the press instead of working, we decline any responsibility in the matter.

Please tell us which items were the most fun to crush.

Excellent. Now that you have Oil, we may proceed with one of our favorite industrial byproducts: <color=green>Tar</color>.

Tar is obtained by boiling and calcining a mixture of Pine Resin, Sawdust, and Oil until it becomes thick, black, and extremely reluctant to wash off.

Configure your <color=green>Alchemist</color> to produce Tar. Note that it must be kept <color=red>warm</color> for proper storage.

This substance is primarily used as a caulking material for more advanced constructions, sealing joints and preventing inconvenient leaks.

In particular, it enables the construction of <color=green>Medium Tanks</color>, which are significantly more efficient at storing liquids than the smaller tanks you have been relying on so far.

It also has several other applications involving people you dislike, but we have been strictly prohibited from discussing them. Please do not do the thing we are not allowed to mention.

It is very fun, though.

Excellent. With oil production, tar preparation, and general chemical competence established, we may now proceed to what we’ve all been waiting for :

TIME TO BLOW SHIT UP !

Erm, please forgive our enthusiasm. You wouldn't believe how boring it is here since they revoked our access to the lab.

To produce Dynamite, you will first need Nitroglycerin. Your <color=green>Alchemist</color> can synthesize it from Sunflower Oil and Saltpeter.

Saltpeter can be obtained from a <color=green>Primitive Mine</color>. You should already have one. If not, please correct this alarming situation immediately.

Nitroglycerin, as you may know, tends to react poorly to sudden movement, loud noises, careless handling, or existence in general.

Have your <color=green>Handicrafter</color> stabilize it with sawdust, then roll it into dynamite sticks for convenient destruction.

Please prepare as many explosives as possible. We are suddenly very interested in field research.

Hello.

I am currently answering messages on behalf of the Directorate of Applied Chemistry and Public Health.

The previous staff appear to have… vacated their positions. Quite suddenly. I really hope they didn't get into trouble again.

The authorities have asked that we immediately report any sightings of funny-smelling chemists who should not be left unsupervised around… well, anything really. Possibly pencils and paper.

Speaking of which, I have found a note instructing me to continue the chemical program. It says: “Next step: Brain-Boosting Salts.”

If I remember my classes correctly, this requires the production of <color=green>Alcohol</color>.

To obtain alcohol, you will first need fermentable ingredients. You may proceed in either of the following ways:

- Plant <color=green>Rice</color> in <color=#00FFFF>shallow water</color> in the river.
- Plant <color=green>Chestnut Trees</color> wherever they might look nice.

Then please construct two additional stacks of Fermentation Barrels and configure them to produce either <color=green>Half-Fermented Sake</color> or <color=green>Chestnut Beer</color>, whichever is appropriate.

Your settlers will probably attempt to drink those, but worry not — the following headaches will quickly teach them moderation.

Good. With fermentation underway, we may now proceed to the next step.

The alcohol produced in your Fermentation Barrels must be refined through distillation.

Construct a Distillery and configure it accordingly.

You may already possess one, as the same facility is commonly used to produce Pollution Resistance Factor. If that is the case, we strongly recommend constructing a second Distillery.

Running out of PRF during a Badtide tends to produce very avoidable embarrassment.

Once <color=green>strong alcohol</color> becomes available, your <color=green>Alchemist</color> will be able to proceed with the preparation of <color=green>Brain-Boosting Salts</color>.

The chemical process is unfortunately classified, though it should have been included in your library set. This is apparently a precautionary measure.

I could tell you why, but I… uuh… would need to review the protocol myself.

I assure you I would never misuse it. Probably.

Congratulations.

Your ability to follow instructions has allowed you to reach the final step of this chemical program. You would be surprised to learn how uncommon that talent is. I certainly was.

Brain-Boosting Salts, when used properly, are a powerful cognitive stimulant. They help trained specialists such as <color=green>architects</color> and <color=green>mechanics</color> remain focused during intellectually demanding work, or simply settlers engaged in study at the <color=green>library</color> — assuming any of them have time for that.

Another practical use of this compound is the construction of an Aromatic Burner.

This structure gently warms the salts and releases stimulating vapors into the surrounding area, allowing nearby beavers to benefit from their effects without the need for direct handling. Direct inhalation of the salts is strongly discouraged, but appears to be statistically unavoidable.

Please construct at least one Aromatic Burner and place it wherever its pleasant aroma seems appropriate.

I hope you do not have further questions because… well, this Directorate appears to be no longer functional.

You might, however, be able to obtain assistance by placing dynamite sticks over a pitfall trap. I found some of your earlier correspondence.

Primitive industry has served its purpose. The next stage requires precision.

This branch concerns the production of <color=green>Gears</color>, expansion of mechanical power networks, and the refinement of industrial systems beyond their initial limitations.

With proper gearing, power may be transmitted further, machinery may be improved, and <color=green>Water Pumps</color> may be upgraded.

When you are prepared to replace improvisation with engineering, follow up on this directive.

Rotation is the lifeforce of machines.

Hello.

We have been informed that your settlement has reached the point where mechanical optimization becomes desirable. This is excellent news. Mechanical optimization is our favorite kind of optimization.

Before we proceed, we must establish a facility dedicated to the analysis and fabrication of mechanical components. In other words: a Mechanics Lodge.

One of the primary functions of this building is the production of <color=green>Gears</color>, which are essential for transmitting rotational force between machines.

You will notice that standard policy is to leave gears and moving parts fully exposed, which some timid individuals describe as “dangerous”. 

Do not let such foolish concerns distract you, people who are injured by moving parts are simply unworthy of the bounty of machines.

Construct a Mechanics Lodge to demonstrate that your settlement is capable of basic mechanical competence.

Excellent.

Let us now introduce a simple but extremely satisfying improvement: Water Pump Upgrades.

These devices dramatically increase the pumping capacity of existing water pumps through the entirely sensible application of additional moving parts.

Before constructing one, you should familiarize yourself with their placement. To do so, place a <color=green>Water Pump Upgrade Board</color> somewhere convenient.

The board does not need to actually be built in order to be consulted. Please do not question how this works. We don't know either and that makes our heads hurt.

If you have properly followed the earlier recommendations of the Directorate of Hydrological Discipline, you should now possess a neat <color=green>row of water pumps</color> ready for improvement.

We advised them to include that step. They resisted at first, but with enough… torque... applied to their arm, they eventually saw the light.

Construct at least one Water Pump Upgrade to prove your willingness to coexist with machines.

Your Water Pump Upgrades are a respectable improvement. We appreciate the effort.

However, they remain crude devices ultimately powered by manual labor.

Technological evolution requires buildings driven by true mechanical power. The most important of these is the Factory.

The Factory is primarily used to refine <color=green>Scrap Metal</color> into proper <color=green>Metal Blocks</color>, which will become necessary for many advanced constructions.

It also serves a number of secondary purposes, such as fabricating <color=green>Anvils</color>, <color=green>Laboratory Glassware</color>, and <color=green>Cauldrons</color>.

In a properly organized industrial settlement, one Factory should ideally produce Metal Blocks continuously, while another handles miscellaneous custom fabrication.

Do not forget that these buildings are appropriately <color=#00FFFF>watertight</color>. Machines do not look kindly upon those who squander opportunities… or torque.

As with most mechanically respectable buildings, the power plug is located at the rear. Ensure the structure is properly connected to your power network.

Construct a Factory so that the worthy may prove themselves — and the unworthy may be identified.

With a Factory in operation, your settlement is now capable of producing a wider range of mechanical improvements.

We recommend upgrading several of your earlier production facilities.

You may proceed in any of the following ways:

- Construct a Proper Papermill (recommended).
- Construct a Proper Ropemaker.
- Construct an Industrial Kitchen.
- Construct a Deep Pumping House, if your ancestral beaver instinct to dam rivers cannot be contained.

Deep Pumping Houses are approximately 33% more efficient than standard pumping structures. Unfortunately, they do not provide the convenient flat roof required for certain structural upgrades. A regrettable compromise. Architects tend to complain about this.

Naturally, we trust that any devout machine enthusiast will build all four.

Your mechanical infrastructure is beginning to show promise.

The next stage will require a more ambitious project: the design of a proper <color=green>Floodgate Dam</color>.

Such a structure allows your settlement to redirect water flow toward — or away from — critical infrastructure, typically to prevent a Badtide from reaching and contaminating your reservoir.

Instruct your <color=green>Mechanic</color> to begin drafting plans for this device. This research will require considerable time and resources, so ensure it has everything required to work without interruption.

Most notably, <color=red>Brain Boosting Salts</color> will be required for such intensive reflection. Contact the <color=red>Directorate of Applied Chemistry</color> and survive their questionable guidance in order to establish production.

When the task is complete, the Mechanic will eventually emerge from the lodge brandishing a perfectly clear and definitely understandable <color=green>blueprint</color> of the invention.

While this process unfolds, we recommend that you follow the instructions of the rather insufferable people from the Bureau of Intellectual Property.

We contacted them on your behalf.

You are welcome.

Ah. You are still alive. Good.

It seems you have successfully produced <color=red>Brain Boosting Salts</color>, and since we — thankfully — did not hear back from the IPP bureau, we will assume you managed to duplicate your blueprints.

You may now construct a Floodgate Dam.

The objective of such a structure is not to stop water entirely — that is the thinking of amateurs and architects — but to redirect its flow according to your needs.

Properly placed floodgates allow you to guide water away from your reservoir during a Badtide, or toward your infrastructure when conditions are favorable.

Construct at least one Floodgate Dam and demonstrate to all that machines are superior to the forces of nature.

Expansion requires support. Height without structure is collapse waiting to happen.

This branch concerns the production of <color=green>Scaffoldings</color> for the construction of <color=green>Platforms</color>, walkways, and reinforced multi-level infrastructure.

Scaffoldings enables vertical growth, <color=green>Farm Upgrades</color>, and enhanced mobility — including <color=green>Zipline transit systems</color> for efficient movement across our territory.

When you are prepared to build higher without falling, follow up on this directive.

Elevation increases possibility. It also increases consequences.

Greetings.

We represent the Directorate of Architectural Ambition, the body responsible for ensuring that settlements rise above crude piles of timber and become structures of elegance.

Your settlement, while… functional… currently demonstrates a worrying absence of architectural vision. Like most diseases, this is correctable.

Build an Architect’s Lodge so that your settlement may take its first step toward dignity.

This building will allow a trained Architect to assemble sturdy yet lightweight <color=green>Scaffoldings</color>, which form the foundation for walkways, platforms, upgrades, and other structural elements that allow settlements to grow vertically, rather than spreading like an undisciplined fungus across the landscape.

Postscript: You may notice that the <color=#FF6EC7>rear façade</color> of the building forms a large angled structure. This is not a <color=#FF6EC7>staircase</color>.

It is an architectural gesture intended to evoke upward motion and structural dynamism. Please do not allow your settlers to walk on it.

Yes, it is possible.

That does not make it acceptable.

Greetings again.

Now that your settlement possesses an Architect’s Lodge, we may begin correcting another of its more regrettable deficiencies: the absence of modular architectural planning.

You may have noticed that some buildings are described as having a <color=#FFA500>Small Tower</color> or a <color=#FF6EC7>Triangle Roof</color>. This is not decorative language. It indicates that these structures are capable of receiving architectural upgrades.

In most cases, upgrades require either <color=#FF6EC7>two triangular roofs placed side by side</color>, or <color=#FFA500>one small tower combined with a triangular roof</color>.

To ensure your limited intellect can grasp the principle, place a <color=green>Modular Upgrade Billboard</color> and consult it.

Once you have understood the principle, construct at least one Farm Assistant Upgrade. Should you feel unusually inspired, any other upgrade will also be acceptable.

Note that upgraded buildings also gain one additional level of <color=#00FFFF>water retention ability</color>. You may exploit this structural advantage as you see fit.

More importantly, upgraded buildings look nice.

Excellent.

Now that you understand the basic principles of scaffolding and modular upgrades, we may address another matter of architectural responsibility: <color=green>covered storage</color>.

These structures protect valuable resources from the elements and, thanks to their flat roofs and sturdy construction, can be conveniently stacked vertically. This allows settlements to store large quantities of materials without spreading storage across the entire landscape like a poorly planned lumber camp.

We recommend that you construct whichever <color=green>covered storage</color> best fits your settlement’s current needs.

A population sitting atop generous reserves tends to remain calm, productive, and most importantly : less inclined to interrupt us  with tiresome requests for spare materials.

Configure both buildings to work on the Floodgate Dam blueprint.

This procedure is perfectly legal, as it only violates the spirit of the regulations.
